mainTopic: מוציא שם רע: why רבי מאיר says 3 judges and the חכמים say 23, explained by עולא, רבא, אביי, רב פפא and רב אשי
overview: In the משנה, רבי מאיר says a מוציא שם רע case is judged by three judges, and the חכמים say twenty-three. Earlier, עולא explained that they argue about worrying for לעז (rumors), and רבא said they argue about כבודן של ראשונים (the honor of the first judges). Here the גמרא brings a ברייתא where the חכמים say a money claim needs only three, which fits רבא but seems hard for עולא. רבא himself, with רב חייא בר אבין, defends עולא: the three-judge money case is the father's claim against the husband after the husband's witnesses were proven עדים זוממין, and the 23-judge case is the trial of those witnesses. Then אביי says everyone holds both concerns, and the argument is about a warning given in general terms, matching a ברייתא where רבי יהודה requires naming the exact death. רב פפא offers another case: a woman learned in Torah (חבירה) who was not warned, which ties to the dispute of רבי יוסי בר יהודה and the רבנן. Finally רב אשי begins yet another explanation, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A ברייתא that fits רבא but challenges עולא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the חכמים in a ברייתא: a money claim needs 3 judges, a capital claim needs 23. This fits רבא's explanation but seems difficult for עולא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: The חכמים say, if he sued her for money, the case is judged by three. If he sued her for her life, it is judged by twenty-three. This works well for רבא: if he first sued for money, three judges; if he first sued for her life, then even the money part stays with twenty-three. But for עולא it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא and shows that it fits רבא's view but causes a problem for עולא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא reads the ברייתא as describing how the case started: a case that began as money needs only 3, and a case that began as capital stays with 23 even after it turns into money, out of respect for the first judges. עולא, however, said the חכמים worry about rumors and require 23 even for a plain money claim. Yet the ברייתא has the חכמים saying a money claim needs only 3, and that is the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: He sued him/her; he brought a claim
A capital case, where a life is at stake
It is difficult; this is a problem

phrases.english: They raised an objection: And the Rabbis say,
if he sued for money, it is judged by three;
if he sued for a capital case, it is judged by twenty-three.
Granted, according to Rava,
if he sued for money at the outset, it is judged by three;
if he sued for a capital case at the outset,
even the money part is judged by twenty-three.
But according to Ulla, it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the earlier explanations of עולא and רבא against a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's explanation that the argument is about worrying for לעז (rumors).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: According to עולא, the חכמים worry about rumors and require 23 even when the husband claims only money. Yet the ברייתא quotes the חכמים saying a money claim is judged by three. For רבא there is no problem: a claim that was money from the start needs 3, and only a case that began as capital stays with 23.

steps.title: רבא defends עולא: two separate trials
steps.stepSummary: רבא and רב חייא בר אבין explain that the ברייתא is describing two different trials: the father's money claim against the husband (3 judges), and the capital trial of the husband's lying witnesses (23 judges).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: I and the lion of the group explained it. And who is that? רב חייא בר אבין. What case are we dealing with here? The husband brought witnesses that she was unfaithful, and the father brought witnesses who proved the husband's witnesses to be עדים זוממין. When the father comes to collect money from the husband, it takes three judges. But for the capital case, it takes twenty-three.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge on behalf of עולא by showing that the ברייתא is talking about two separate trials.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'money' case in the ברייתא is not an ordinary money claim. It is the father collecting the fine from the husband after the husband's witnesses were proven עדים זוממין. Her name is already cleared, so there is no rumor to worry about, and 3 judges are enough. The 'capital' case is the trial of those lying witnesses, who now face death, so it needs 23. The ברייתא therefore does not contradict עולא's claim that in an ordinary money claim the חכמים require 23 because of rumors.

keyTerms.meaning: The lion of the group; a title of honor for a great scholar
What case are we dealing with here?
They proved them to be עדים זוממין (lying witnesses who were somewhere else)

steps.confusionAlert: It is רבא himself who is defending עולא here, even though עולא disagrees with him. Do not read this as רבא defending his own view.

phrases.english: Rava said:
I and the lion of the group explained it.
And who is he? Rav Ḥiyya bar Avin.
With what are we dealing here?
Where the husband brought witnesses that she committed adultery,
and the father brought witnesses
and they proved the husband's witnesses to be conspiring witnesses.
If he comes to collect money from the husband, it is by three;
phrases.notes: "He" is the father, collecting the fine from the husband for falsely shaming his daughter.

phrases.english: and in a capital matter, it is by twenty-three.
phrases.notes: This means the trial of the husband's lying witnesses, who now face the death penalty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: אֲנִי וַאֲרִי שֶׁבַּחֲבוּרָה תַּרְגֵּימְנַהּ
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the case: the ברייתא describes two separate trials, not one trial that changes.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say that the חכמים allow an ordinary money claim against the wife to be judged by three, which goes against עולא.
steps.terutzMaskana: The money trial (father against husband) needs 3, and the separate capital trial (against the עדים זוממין) needs 23, so nothing contradicts עולא.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the גמרא can save a view by narrowing the case of a ברייתא, even through the words of the opposing אמורא.

steps.title: אביי: everyone agrees; the argument is about a general warning
steps.stepSummary: אביי says everyone worries both about rumors and about the honor of the first judges. The argument between רבי מאיר and חכמים is about a case where the witnesses warned her without saying which death she would get.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Everyone agrees we worry about rumors and about the honor of the first judges. What case are we dealing with here? Where they warned her in a general way.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers a completely different way to explain the argument between רבי מאיר and the חכמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike עולא and רבא, אביי says the two concerns are not the subject of the argument at all, because everyone holds both. Instead, the question is whether a general warning (just 'you will be killed', without naming the type of death) counts. If it counts, she is truly facing a capital case and needs 23; if it does not count, there is no death penalty and only the money claim remains, needing 3.

keyTerms.meaning: We worry about rumors / a bad name
The honor of the first judges

phrases.english: Abaye said:
According to everyone, we are concerned about rumors,
and about the honor of the first judges.
With what are we dealing here?
Such as where they warned her without specification.
phrases.notes: They told her she would be killed, but didn't say which kind of death.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַבָּיֵי אָמַר: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא חָיְישִׁינַן לְלַעַז
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the עולא/רבא debate and offers a third explanation of the argument.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New framing of the argument: from rumor/honor concerns to whether a general warning is valid.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The argument between רבי מאיר and חכמים was thought to be about rumors or about the first judges' honor.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everyone holds both concerns; the argument is about a case where the התראה was given in general terms.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the number of judges in מוציא שם רע to the basic laws of התראה needed for any death penalty.

steps.title: A תנא who fits אביי's case of a general warning
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that the idea of a general warning matches a known תנא: a ברייתא requires that the person be told he is liable to death in court, without saying he must be told which death.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this follows a certain תנא, as it was taught in a ברייתא: All the other people in the תורה who are liable to death are put to death only with a court, witnesses, and a warning, and only once they have told him that he is liable to death in court.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא grounds אביי's case in a known dispute among the תנאים by quoting a ברייתא. Its first opinion requires only telling the sinner he is liable to death. The opposing opinion of רבי יהודה comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This ברייתא lists what is needed before an execution: a court, witnesses, a warning, and telling the sinner he is liable to death. It only requires telling him 'you are liable to death', not which kind, so it fits the view that a general warning counts. This shows that אביי's case reflects a real opinion among the תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: People liable to the death penalty
A warning given just before the sin

phrases.english: And it is in accordance with this tanna, as it is taught:
And all the others liable for death penalties in the Torah,
they do not put them to death
except with a congregation, witnesses, and forewarning,
and only once they inform him
that he is liable to death in court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Grounds אביי's case of a general warning in an opinion of a תנא.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's case: an argument about whether a general warning counts.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא listing what is required for execution, which only requires telling the sinner he is liable to death in court.
steps.whatToRemember: So far there are three ways to explain the argument about מוציא שם רע: עולא (rumors), רבא (honor of the first judges), and אביי (everyone agrees on both; the question is a general התראה). רב פפא and רב אשי add more explanations below.

steps.title: רבי יהודה requires naming the exact death penalty
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי יהודה says a person is not executed unless he was told exactly which death penalty he would get. This is the other side of the dispute, matching רבי מאיר in אביי's explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: He is not killed until they tell him by which death he will be killed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא from the last step. Now we hear the opposing opinion, רבי יהודה, who demands a specific warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 4 the first opinion said a general warning ('you will get death in court') is enough. רבי יהודה disagrees: the witnesses must name the exact death. So אביי's idea works: רבי מאיר holds like רבי יהודה, so a general warning cannot lead to death, and the case needs only 3 judges. The חכמים hold like the first opinion, so the case is capital and needs 23.
steps.whatToRemember: According to אביי: רבי מאיר = רבי יהודה (a warning must name the specific death). חכמים = the first opinion (a general warning is enough).

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
He is not executed until they inform him
by which death he is to be killed.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עַד שֶׁיּוֹדִיעוּהוּ בְּאֵיזֹה מִיתָה הוּא נֶהֱרָג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in step 4, supplying the opinion that matches רבי מאיר.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's explanation that the dispute is about a general versus a specific warning.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's dispute: the first opinion (general warning is enough) against רבי יהודה (a specific warning is needed).

steps.title: רב פפא: the case is about a Torah-knowledgeable woman
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא offers a different explanation: the case involves a woman who is a חבירה, and רבי מאיר and the חכמים disagree the same way רבי יוסי בר יהודה and the רבנן disagree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Here we are dealing with a woman who is a חבירה, and they disagree in the same way as the dispute between רבי יוסי בר יהודה and the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a second way to explain why רבי מאיר says only 3 judges. He says the woman is someone who knows Torah law well.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the woman knows the law, do the witnesses still need to warn her? According to רב פפא, רבי מאיר holds like the רבנן, who say even a learned person needs a warning. Here she was not warned, so she cannot be put to death, and only 3 judges are needed. The חכמים hold like רבי יוסי בר יהודה: a learned person needs no warning, so the case could be capital and needs 23.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is learned in Torah law

steps.confusionAlert: Watch the matching carefully: רבי מאיר (3 judges) = the רבנן (a חבר needs a warning). The חכמים (23 judges) = רבי יוסי בר יהודה (a חבר needs no warning).

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Here we are dealing with a woman who is a חבירה,
phrases.notes: A חבירה is a woman who knows Torah law well, so she clearly knew the act was forbidden.

phrases.english: and they disagree

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְלוּגְתָּא דְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה וְרַבָּנַן.
phrases.english: in the same dispute as Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda and the Rabbis.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: הָכָא בְּאִשָּׁה חֲבֵירָה עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another explanation of the dispute between רבי מאיר and the חכמים, standing alongside אביי's explanation in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the woman was a learned חבירה who was not warned.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think רבי מאיר's 3 judges must be explained through the type of warning, as אביי said.
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute can also be about whether a learned person needs any warning at all.

steps.title: The source: a learned person needs no warning, says רבי יוסי בר יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says a חבר does not need a warning, because a warning is only meant to separate an accidental sinner from a deliberate one.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי יוסי בר יהודה says: A חבר does not need a warning, because a warning was only given to tell apart someone who sins by mistake from someone who sins on purpose.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the ברייתא that רב פפא is relying on, to show this dispute really exists.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי בר יהודה explains the purpose of a warning: to prove the person knew what he was doing. A learned person surely knows, so the warning is not needed. The רבנן (not quoted here) disagree and require a warning for everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: A person learned in Torah law
A warning given before the sin

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that, for רבי יוסי בר יהודה, a warning is only a tool to prove the person knew. If we already know, the tool is not needed.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a ברייתא:
Rabbi Yosei bar Yehuda says:
A חבר does not need a warning,
because a warning was given
only to tell apart someone who sins by mistake from someone who sins on purpose.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בַּר יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: חָבֵר אֵין צָרִיךְ הַתְרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the ברייתא source for the dispute רב פפא mentioned.
steps.raayaObject: רב פפא's claim that there is a known dispute about whether a חבר needs a warning.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא with רבי יוסי בר יהודה's opinion and his reason.

steps.title: רב אשי begins a third explanation
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי starts to give another explanation of the case, beginning with 'for example, where...'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: For example, where...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a third answer, from רב אשי. He starts describing a specific case, and the details continue on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After אביי and רב פפא, רב אשי gives yet another way to explain why רבי מאיר needs only 3 judges. The word כגון tells us he is about to describe a particular situation.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said: For example, where

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a third alternative answer after אביי and רב פפא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think the only explanations are those of אביי and רב פפא.
steps.terutzMaskana: Not yet stated; רב אשי's case is explained on the next amud.
